_: ⭐⭐⭐ THE SYMBOL-SCOPED VOCABULARY — what `syminfo.*` may resolve to, and where the vendor's own spelling lands when it is measured. This is the FOURTH kind of dotted Pine name (engine-model constants → `BUILTIN_CONSTANT_TREE`; calendar constants → `BUILTIN_CALENDAR_TREE`; series aliases → `BUILTIN_TIMEFRAME_ALIAS`; and these). It is a DATA FILE rather than a map in `pine.js` because every value in it is a fact about the outside world — our symbol store's vocabulary on one side, TradingView's on the other — and neither is a property of the grammar. A fact that can change without any code changing belongs where it can be edited without reading code.
_the_one_rule: ⛔⛔ AN UNCONFIRMED SPELLING IS NEVER SERVED. `syminfo.exchange` and `syminfo.tickerid` are TRADINGVIEW STRINGS, not ours: the member's script compares them with `==` and `str.contains`, so a plausible-but-unmeasured spelling does not degrade the answer, it INVERTS it. `NASDAQ` vs `NASDAQ Global Select` vs `NMS` are three different answers to `syminfo.exchange == "NASDAQ"` and only one of them is the vendor's. So the serving path reads `confirmed` and nothing else; `store_to_pine` below is a PROPOSAL that serves nothing until a capture backs it.
_why_not_just_ship_our_own_spelling: Because it would be a KNOWN WRONG VALUE, which this program does not ship. Our store's `exchange` field holds trader-friendly names (`NYSE Arca`, `NASDAQ Global Select`) assembled from yfinance MIC-ish codes and FMP free text — see `_YF_EXCHANGE` in `api/services/ticker_meta.py`. Handing one of those to a script that tests `syminfo.exchange == "AMEX"` answers false where TradingView answers true, silently, per symbol, forever.
_what_ships_today: ⭐ ALL THREE OF `syminfo.ticker`, `syminfo.tickerid` and `syminfo.exchange` are Kind-4 NAMES — the door resolves each to a `symtext` node — and the six fields in `unserved` refuse BY NAME at the door. The gate on the two vendor-spelled fields is NOT the door, it is the FOLD, and it is per-binding: `syminfo.ticker` folds for every symbol, while `tickerid` and `exchange` fold only for a symbol whose exchange has a `confirmed` entry below. ⭐⭐ THAT IS WHY THE GATE LIVES IN THE FOLD: confirmation is a property of THE SYMBOL'S EXCHANGE, decided when a symbol is chosen, and a door that runs once per script cannot decide it. It also means a capture turns these on with NO CODE CHANGE — the mechanism is built, railed and reachable today, and the only thing missing is the measurement.
_the_probe_that_settles_it: On a live TradingView chart, for each symbol below: `plot(0)` with `str.tostring(syminfo.exchange)` and `str.tostring(syminfo.tickerid)` in a label, or read `syminfo` off the chart model directly (see `lesson_a_tradingview_chart_answers_in_numbers_not_pixels` — a live TV chart exposes its whole model on `window`). Record each capture as a `confirmed` entry with the date and how it was taken. One capture per DISTINCT store spelling is enough; the map is per-exchange, not per-symbol.

confirmed._: ⛔ EMPTY ON PURPOSE, AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE. Nothing here has been measured against TradingView yet, so nothing here is served. Each entry is `<our store's exchange string>`: `{pine, witness, captured, how}` — `pine` is the string TradingView's `syminfo.exchange` returns, `witness` the symbol it was read on, `captured` the date, `how` the method. ⚠️ A future entry MUST carry all four: an entry without a witness is an assertion wearing a data structure.

store_to_pine._: ⚠️ A PROPOSAL, NOT A MAPPING IN FORCE. These are the pairings we EXPECT the capture to confirm, written down so the probe knows what to check and so a reviewer can disagree with a specific line rather than with a vacuum. The serving path does not read this object. Moving a line from here into `confirmed` requires a witness.

_the_store_vocabulary_is_not_closed: ⚠️ AND IT CANNOT BE MADE CLOSED FROM HERE. `_YF_EXCHANGE` in `api/services/ticker_meta.py` is a bounded set and a rail checks this file covers every value of it. FMP's leg is not bounded — `row.get('exchange') or row.get('exchangeShortName')` is free text from a vendor — so a symbol can arrive carrying an exchange string nothing here names. THAT SYMBOL REFUSES rather than guessing, which is the same failure direction as everything else in this file.

unserved._: ⛔ THE `syminfo.*` FIELDS THAT ARE REFUSED BY NAME, each with the reason a member can act on. A generic `pine:builtin` — *"the engine grammar does not hold this"* — would be FALSE the moment `syminfo.ticker` works one line above, and a refusal that is false about its neighbours teaches the reader to distrust every refusal.
unserved.type: what kind of instrument the symbol is (`stock`, `futures`, `crypto`…). This engine screens US equities, so the answer would be the same constant for every symbol it can reach — a value that cannot vary is not a value, it is a hidden assumption, and a script branching on it would take one arm forever without being told why.
unserved.currency: the symbol's quote currency. Same shape as `type`: constant across everything this engine holds, so serving it would let a multi-currency script look like it was working while one whole branch was unreachable.
unserved.session: the symbol's trading session string. This engine evaluates the bars it is given and holds no session calendar per symbol, so there is nothing here to read it from.
unserved.mintick: It is the symbol's minimum price increment, which differs per symbol and is not something this engine holds. ⭐ IN PRACTICE IT APPEARS IN ONE IDIOM — `math.max(high - low, syminfo.mintick)` — a guard against dividing by a bar whose range is zero. THIS ENGINE DOES NOT NEED THAT GUARD: a zero denominator is reported as NOT COMPUTABLE for that symbol rather than quietly replaced, so write `(close - low) / (high - low)` and a halted, zero-range bar is left unanswered instead of being scored as though it closed on its low. ⚠️ That is a REAL difference, not a simplification: Pine answers 0 on such a bar and this engine answers nothing, which is why the edit is yours to make rather than one taken silently on your behalf.
unserved.pointvalue: the currency value of one point, which is a contract specification for futures and is not something this engine holds for the equities it screens.
unserved.description: the instrument's long name. It is free text from a data vendor, it differs between our providers for the same symbol, and a script that branches on it would branch on which provider answered — the definition of a value that is not reproducible.

_why_unserved_is_a_ROSTER_and_not_a_defa: ⛔ BECAUSE A DEFAULT CANNOT BE COUNTED. A namespace-wide fallthrough would refuse an unknown `syminfo.whatever` with the same sentence as `syminfo.mintick`, and nobody could tell from the outside which names had been THOUGHT ABOUT and which had merely fallen through. The roster is the thinking; the fallthrough stays behind it for names nobody has ruled on yet.

pending_measurement._: ⛔ THE REASON THE FOLD QUOTES when one of these cannot be resolved for a binding. It is a MEASUREMENT gap, not a grammar gap, and the sentence has to say so — a member reading "the engine grammar does not hold this" would rewrite a script that will work unchanged the day a witness lands.
pending_measurement.tickerid: the exchange-prefixed identifier — `EXCHANGE:SYMBOL`. The symbol half is ours; the exchange half is a TradingView string this engine has not measured, and a comparison against a guessed prefix answers backwards rather than approximately. Waiting on the capture described in `_the_probe_that_settles_it`. ⭐ IF YOU ONLY NEED TO KNOW WHETHER THE SYMBOL IS A PAIR OR RATIO CHART, `syminfo.ticker` already answers that and is served.
pending_measurement.exchange: the exchange code — a TradingView string this engine has not measured. Our symbol store holds a trader-friendly name (`NYSE Arca`) which is not what Pine returns, and serving it would answer `syminfo.exchange == "AMEX"` false where TradingView answers true. Waiting on the same capture.
